q: About _____ of the mass of the Earth's crust consists of oxygen.
e: About 50% of the mass of the Earth's crust consists of oxygen. 50% is the idea that completes this fact. 21% would fill a different blank than 50%.

q: The free element of oxygen accounts for _____ of the volume of the atmosphere.
e: The free element of oxygen accounts for 21% of the volume of the atmosphere. Free oxygen gas makes up about 21 percent of dry air by volume. 50% would fill a different blank than 21%.

q: In the laboratory, oxygen gas can be prepared by using an environmentally friendly liquid _____ of appropriate strength.
e: In the laboratory, oxygen gas can be prepared by using an environmentally friendly liquid hydrogen peroxide of appropriate strength. Hydrogen is the lightest element and a common fuel and reducing agent in the lab. Water would fill a different blank than hydrogen peroxide.

q: In the preparation of oxygen from hydrogen peroxide, _____ is used as a catalyst to speed up the chemical reaction.
e: In the preparation of oxygen from hydrogen peroxide, manganese(IV) oxide is used as a catalyst to speed up the chemical reaction. Manganese(IV) oxide is the idea that completes this fact. Potassium chlorate would fill a different blank than manganese(IV) oxide.

q: Oxygen gas is collected by the _____ of water.
e: Oxygen gas is collected by the downward displacement of water. Downward displacement is the idea that completes this fact. Downward delivery would fill a different blank than downward displacement.

q: The chemical equation for the preparation of oxygen from hydrogen peroxide is _____.
e: The chemical equation for the preparation of oxygen from hydrogen peroxide is 2H2O2(aq) MnO2 2H2O(l) + O2(g). 2H2O2(aq) MnO2 2H2O(l) + O2(g) is the idea that completes this fact. H2O2(aq) MnO2 H2O(l) + O2(g) would fill a different blank than 2H2O2(aq) MnO2 2H2O(l) + O2(g).

q: Oxygen is a colourless gas, without taste or smell, and is only _____ soluble in water.
e: Oxygen is a colourless gas, without taste or smell, and is only slightly soluble in water. Slightly is the idea that completes this fact. Completely would fill a different blank than slightly.

q: Oxygen will not burn, however, it _____ combustion.
e: Oxygen will not burn, however, it supports combustion. Oxygen supports respiration and combustion, and it is a very reactive non-metal. Prevents is among the listed items, so it is not the exception.

q: Oxygen rekindles any glowing thing (splinter) with a _____.
e: Oxygen rekindles any glowing thing (splinter) with a bright flame. Bright flame is the idea that completes this fact. Dazzling white flame would fill a different blank than bright flame.

q: When magnesium burns in oxygen from air, it leaves a white powder residue which is _____.
e: When magnesium burns in oxygen from air, it leaves a white powder residue which is magnesium oxide. Magnesium oxide is the idea that completes this fact. Magnesium hydroxide would fill a different blank than magnesium oxide.

q: The chemical equation for the burning of magnesium ribbon in oxygen is _____.
e: The chemical equation for the burning of magnesium ribbon in oxygen is 2Mg(s) + O2(g) 2MgO(s). 2Mg(s) + O2(g) 2MgO(s) is the idea that completes this fact. 2Mg(s) + O2(g) Mg2O(s) would fill a different blank than 2Mg(s) + O2(g) 2MgO(s).

q: Iron slowly becomes oxidised in the presence of air and water to form hydrated iron(III) oxide, which is commonly known as _____.
e: Iron slowly becomes oxidised in the presence of air and water to form hydrated iron(III) oxide, which is commonly known as rust. Rust is the idea that completes this fact. Bauxite would fill a different blank than rust.

q: Non-metals such as phosphorus, sulphur and carbon react with oxygen forming _____.
e: Non-metals such as phosphorus, sulphur and carbon react with oxygen forming oxides. Oxides is the idea that completes this fact. Chlorides would fill a different blank than oxides.

q: Red phosphorus burns in oxygen giving off white fumes which consist of _____.
e: Red phosphorus burns in oxygen giving off white fumes which consist of oxides of phosphorus. Oxides of phosphorus is the idea that completes this fact. Phosphorus hydride would fill a different blank than oxides of phosphorus.

q: An acidic oxide is an oxide of _____.
e: An acidic oxide is an oxide of non-metal. Acidic oxides are usually non-metal oxides that make acids with water or react with bases. Metalloid would fill a different blank than non-metal.

q: An acidic oxide reacts with basic oxides to give _____ only.
e: An acidic oxide reacts with basic oxides to give salts only. Basic oxides are usually metal oxides that react with acids to make salt and water. Salts and water would fill a different blank than salts.

q: Acidic oxides react with alkali solutions to give _____.
e: Acidic oxides react with alkali solutions to give salts and water. Salts and water is the idea that completes this fact. Salts and hydrogen would fill a different blank than salts and water.

q: The test for carbon dioxide involves passing it into calcium hydroxide solution, which turns milky due to the formation of _____.
e: The test for carbon dioxide involves passing it into calcium hydroxide solution, which turns milky due to the formation of calcium carbonate. Calcium carbonate is the idea that completes this fact. Calcium bicarbonate would fill a different blank than calcium carbonate.

q: Among the following, the insoluble acidic oxide is _____.
e: Among the following, the insoluble acidic oxide is SiO2. SiO2 is the idea that completes this fact. CO2 would fill a different blank than SiO2.

q: Soluble acidic oxides dissolve in water to form acidic solutions. These solutions turn blue litmus _____.
e: Soluble acidic oxides dissolve in water to form acidic solutions. These solutions turn blue litmus red. Red is the idea that completes this fact. Blue would fill a different blank than red.

q: A basic oxide is an oxide of _____.
e: A basic oxide is an oxide of metal. Metal is the idea that completes this fact. Non-metal would fill a different blank than metal.

q: A basic oxide reacts with an acid to produce _____.
e: A basic oxide reacts with an acid to produce a salt and water only. A salt and water only is the idea that completes this fact. An acid and water only would fill a different blank than a salt and water only.

q: Among the following, the insoluble basic oxide is _____.
e: Among the following, the insoluble basic oxide is MgO. MgO is the idea that completes this fact. K2O would fill a different blank than MgO.

q: Some basic oxides react with water forming hydroxide solutions (alkalis). These solutions turn red litmus _____.
e: Some basic oxides react with water forming hydroxide solutions (alkalis). These solutions turn red litmus blue. Blue is the idea that completes this fact. Red would fill a different blank than blue.

q: An amphoteric oxide is a metallic oxide which possesses _____.
e: An amphoteric oxide is a metallic oxide which possesses both basic and acidic properties. A property is physical if measuring it leaves the substance itself unchanged, and chemical if composition changes. Only acidic properties would fill a different blank than both basic and acidic properties.

q: An amphoteric oxide reacts with both acids and alkalis to form _____.
e: An amphoteric oxide reacts with both acids and alkalis to form salt and water. Salt and water is the idea that completes this fact. Salt and hydrogen would fill a different blank than salt and water.

q: Which of the following is an example of an amphoteric oxide?
e: ZnO is an example of an amphoteric oxide. An amphoteric oxide, such as ZnO, can react with both acids and bases. CO2 is not an example of an amphoteric oxide.

q: A neutral oxide is an oxide which shows _____.
e: A neutral oxide is an oxide which shows neither basic nor acidic character. Neither basic nor acidic character is the idea that completes this fact. Both basic and acidic character would fill a different blank than neither basic nor acidic character.

q: Which of the following is an example of a neutral oxide?
e: CO is an example of a neutral oxide. A neutral oxide such as CO or N2O does not form an acid or a base with water. CO2 is not an example of a neutral oxide.

q: Peroxides are oxides that react with an acid to give salt and _____.
e: Peroxides are oxides that react with an acid to give salt and hydrogen peroxide. Hydrogen is the lightest element and a common fuel and reducing agent in the lab. Hydrogen gas would fill a different blank than hydrogen peroxide.

q: Which of the following is an example of a peroxide?
e: BaO2 is an example of a peroxide. A peroxide contains an O-O link, as in H2O2 or BaO2. MnO2 is not an example of a peroxide.

q: $PbO_2$, $MnO_2$ and $NO_2$ are not peroxides because they _____.
a: do not give hydrogen peroxides on reaction with acids
e: PbO2, MnO2 and NO2 are not peroxides because they do not give hydrogen peroxides on reaction with acids. Hydrogen is the lightest element and a common fuel and reducing agent in the lab. Do not react with acids is among the listed items, so it is not the exception.

q: A compound oxide is an oxide, formed by the combination of two different oxides of the _____.
e: A compound oxide is an oxide, formed by the combination of two different oxides of the same element. An element is a substance made of only one kind of atom. Same compound would fill a different blank than same element.

q: Which of the following is an example of a compound oxide?
e: Pb3O4 is an example of a compound oxide. A compound oxide behaves as if two oxides are combined, like Pb3O4. MgO is not an example of a compound oxide.

q: $Pb_3O_4$ can be written as di-lead(II) lead(IV) oxide or _____.
e: Pb3O4 can be written as di-lead(II) lead(IV) oxide or red lead oxide. Red lead oxide is the idea that completes this fact. Black lead oxide would fill a different blank than red lead oxide.

q: When red lead oxide reacts with dilute nitric acid, only _____ reacts with the acid to form lead(II) nitrate.
e: When red lead oxide reacts with dilute nitric acid, only lead(II) oxide reacts with the acid to form lead(II) nitrate. Lead(II) oxide is the idea that completes this fact. Lead(IV) oxide would fill a different blank than lead(II) oxide.

q: In living organisms, the oxygen intake is used for the breakdown of the _____ molecules to produce energy.
e: In living organisms, the oxygen intake is used for the breakdown of the glucose molecules to produce energy. Glucose is the idea that completes this fact. Protein would fill a different blank than glucose.

q: Liquid oxygen is carried on rockets to _____.
e: Liquid oxygen is carried on rockets to support the fuel burns. A fuel is a substance that releases useful energy as it changes chemically, usually by burning. Cool the engine would fill a different blank than support the fuel burns.

q: Which oxide is used in fire extinguishers?
e: CO2 is oxide is used in fire extinguishers. CO2 is the idea that completes this fact. MgO is a different claim from CO2.

q: Which oxide is used as a bleaching agent?
e: SO2 is oxide is used as a bleaching agent. SO2 is the idea that completes this fact. CO2 is a different claim from SO2.

q: Carbon is found in nature as diamond and _____.
e: Carbon is found in nature as diamond and graphite. Graphite is the idea that completes this fact. Graphene would fill a different blank than graphite.

q: Fullerene and graphene are _____ carbon.
e: Fullerene and graphene are synthetic carbon. Synthetic is the idea that completes this fact. Metallic would fill a different blank than synthetic.

q: If an element can exist in more than one form, in the same physical state, it is said to exhibit _____.
e: If an element can exist in more than one form, in the same physical state, it is said to exhibit allotropy or polymorphism. Allotropy or polymorphism is the idea that completes this fact. Isomerism would fill a different blank than allotropy or polymorphism.

q: The different forms of an element in the same physical state that possess different physical properties are known as _____.
e: The different forms of an element in the same physical state that possess different physical properties are known as allotropes. Allotropes are different forms of the same element, such as oxygen and ozone, or diamond and graphite. Isotopes would fill a different blank than allotropes.

q: Which of the following are allotropes of carbon?
e: Diamond, graphite, fullerene and graphene are allotropes of carbon. Diamond, graphite, fullerene and graphene is the idea that completes this fact. Oxygen and ozone are not allotropes of carbon.

q: In diamond, each carbon atom is surrounded by _____ other carbon atoms.
e: In diamond, each carbon atom is surrounded by four other carbon atoms. Four is the idea that completes this fact. Three would fill a different blank than four.

q: Diamond has a giant structure containing millions of carbon atoms in a three dimensional network of strong _____.
e: Diamond has a giant structure containing millions of carbon atoms in a three dimensional network of strong carbon-carbon covalent bonds. A covalent bond forms when atoms share electron pairs. Ionic bonds would fill a different blank than carbon-carbon covalent bonds.

q: The melting point of diamond is _____.
e: The melting point of diamond is 3550 °C. 3550 °C is the idea that completes this fact. 3000 °C would fill a different blank than 3550 °C.

q: Diamond is the _____ among all naturally occurring substances.
e: Diamond is the hardest among all naturally occurring substances. Hardest is the idea that completes this fact. Most conductive would fill a different blank than hardest.

q: In graphite, each carbon atom is surrounded by _____ other carbon atoms in the same plane.
e: In graphite, each carbon atom is surrounded by three other carbon atoms in the same plane. Three is the idea that completes this fact. Four would fill a different blank than three.

q: In graphite, layers of hexagons are weakly bonded to each other through weak forces known as _____.
e: In graphite, layers of hexagons are weakly bonded to each other through weak forces known as van der Waals forces. Van der Waals forces is the idea that completes this fact. Ionic bonds would fill a different blank than van der Waals forces.

q: Due to its layered structure, graphite is soft and has a _____ touch.
e: Due to its layered structure, graphite is soft and has a soapy touch. Soapy is the idea that completes this fact. Metallic would fill a different blank than soapy.

q: Graphite is a good conductor of electricity and heat due to the presence of _____.
e: Graphite is a good conductor of electricity and heat due to the presence of free electrons. An electron is a tiny negative particle that occupies shells around the nucleus. Protons would fill a different blank than free electrons.

q: The melting point of graphite is _____.
e: The melting point of graphite is 3700 °C. 3700 °C is the idea that completes this fact. 3000 °C would fill a different blank than 3700 °C.

q: Fullerene ($C_{60}$) is an allotrope of carbon in the form of a _____.
a: hollow sphere, ellipsoid, tube and many other shapes
e: Fullerene (C60) is an allotrope of carbon in the form of a hollow sphere, ellipsoid, tube and many other shapes. Hollow sphere, ellipsoid, tube and many other shapes is the idea that completes this fact. Single layer of hexagons would fill a different blank than hollow sphere, ellipsoid, tube and many other shapes.

q: Spherical fullerenes are also referred to as _____.
e: Spherical fullerenes are also referred to as Bucky balls. Bucky balls is the idea that completes this fact. Graphene sheets would fill a different blank than Bucky balls.

q: Fullerenes have _____ melting and boiling points than diamond and graphite.
e: Fullerenes have lower melting and boiling points than diamond and graphite. Lower is the idea that completes this fact. Higher would fill a different blank than lower.

q: Graphene is a _____ of graphite.
e: Graphene is a single layer (monolayer) of graphite. Single layer (monolayer) is the idea that completes this fact. Thick block would fill a different blank than single layer (monolayer).

q: Graphene's crystalline structure is _____.
e: Graphene's crystalline structure is two-dimensional. Two-dimensional is the idea that completes this fact. One-dimensional would fill a different blank than two-dimensional.

q: In proportion to its thickness, graphene is about _____ stronger than the strongest steel.
e: In proportion to its thickness, graphene is about 100 times stronger than the strongest steel. 100 times is the idea that completes this fact. 1000 times would fill a different blank than 100 times.

q: Charcoal is made by heating wood in the _____.
e: Charcoal is made by heating wood in the absence of air. Absence of air is the idea that completes this fact. Presence of excess air would fill a different blank than absence of air.

q: Charcoal has a _____ structure and has many small holes.
e: Charcoal has a porous structure and has many small holes. Porous is the idea that completes this fact. Metallic would fill a different blank than porous.

q: Coke is formed by heating coal in the absence of air and is almost _____.
e: Coke is formed by heating coal in the absence of air and is almost pure carbon. Pure carbon is the idea that completes this fact. Pure sulphur would fill a different blank than pure carbon.

q: Carbon black (soot) is left as a residue when kerosene is burnt in a _____ amount of air.
e: Carbon black (soot) is left as a residue when kerosene is burnt in a limited amount of air. Limited is the idea that completes this fact. Sufficient would fill a different blank than limited.

q: When carbon burns in excess air or oxygen, _____ is formed.
e: When carbon burns in excess air or oxygen, carbon dioxide is formed. Carbon dioxide is the idea that completes this fact. Carbon monoxide would fill a different blank than carbon dioxide.

q: When carbon burns in a limited amount of air or oxygen, _____ is formed.
e: When carbon burns in a limited amount of air or oxygen, carbon monoxide is formed. Carbon monoxide is the idea that completes this fact. Carbon dioxide would fill a different blank than carbon monoxide.

q: Carbon can be used as a _____ in the extraction of some metals.
e: Carbon can be used as a reducing agent in the extraction of some metals. Reducing agent is the idea that completes this fact. Oxidising agent would fill a different blank than reducing agent.

q: When strongly heated, carbon can reduce the oxides of zinc to zinc and _____.
e: When strongly heated, carbon can reduce the oxides of zinc to zinc and carbon monoxide. Carbon monoxide is the idea that completes this fact. Carbon dioxide would fill a different blank than carbon monoxide.

q: Diamond is used for jewellery because of its _____.
e: Diamond is used for jewellery because of its brilliant shine. Brilliant shine is the idea that completes this fact. Electrical conductivity would fill a different blank than brilliant shine.

q: Powdered graphite is used as a dry lubricant for machine parts which operate at high temperature because graphite is _____.
e: Powdered graphite is used as a dry lubricant for machine parts which operate at high temperature because graphite is non-volatile. Non-volatile is the idea that completes this fact. Soluble in water would fill a different blank than non-volatile.

q: Fullerene is used in artificial photosynthesis, cosmetics, surface coating of medical devices and _____.
e: Fullerene is used in artificial photosynthesis, cosmetics, surface coating of medical devices and drug delivery system. Drug delivery system is the idea that completes this fact. Printing ink would fill a different blank than drug delivery system.

q: Graphene is widely used for solar cells, light-emitting diodes (LED), touch panels and _____.
e: Graphene is widely used for solar cells, light-emitting diodes (LED), touch panels and smart windows or phones. Smart windows or phones is the idea that completes this fact. Printing ink would fill a different blank than smart windows or phones.

q: Activated charcoal is used as an adsorbent in industry for bleaching, deodourization and _____.
e: Activated charcoal is used as an adsorbent in industry for bleaching, deodourization and water purification. Water purification is the idea that completes this fact. Metal extraction would fill a different blank than water purification.

q: Coke is used as a fuel in the metal industry and as a reducing agent in the extraction of metals such as _____.
e: Coke is used as a fuel in the metal industry and as a reducing agent in the extraction of metals such as lead, iron and zinc. Lead, iron and zinc is the idea that completes this fact. Gold, silver and platinum would fill a different blank than lead, iron and zinc.

q: Carbon black is used for making printing ink, black shoes polish and as a filler in _____.
a: vehicle tyres and other rubber products
e: Carbon black is used for making printing ink, black shoes polish and as a filler in vehicle tyres and other rubber products. Vehicle tyres and other rubber products is the idea that completes this fact. Glass manufacture would fill a different blank than vehicle tyres and other rubber products.

q: Carbon is found in nature combined with other elements in petroleum, coal, natural gas, limestone, carbon dioxide and _____.
e: Carbon is found in nature combined with other elements in petroleum, coal, natural gas, limestone, carbon dioxide and sugar. Sugar is the idea that completes this fact. Salt would fill a different blank than sugar.

q: Carbon is a major component of giant molecules called macromolecules which include proteins, lipids, nucleic acids and _____.
e: Carbon is a major component of giant molecules called macromolecules which include proteins, lipids, nucleic acids and carbohydrates. Carbohydrates is the idea that completes this fact. Minerals would fill a different blank than carbohydrates.

q: Graphite is used in making _____ in the cells.
e: Graphite is used in making electrode in the cells. Electrode is the idea that completes this fact. Separator would fill a different blank than electrode.

q: Graphite crucibles are used as containers for _____ at high temperature.
e: Graphite crucibles are used as containers for melting metals at high temperature. Melting is solid to liquid as particles gain energy and leave their fixed places. Boiling water would fill a different blank than melting metals.

q: A very small amount of carbon is used to make some types of _____.
e: A very small amount of carbon is used to make some types of steel. Steel is the idea that completes this fact. Cement would fill a different blank than steel.

q: Charcoal is commonly used as a fuel for _____.
e: Charcoal is commonly used as a fuel for cooking. Cooking changes substances in food, so it is everyday chemistry. Driving cars would fill a different blank than cooking.

q: Carbon black is used for making _____ and black shoes polish.
e: Carbon black is used for making printing ink and black shoes polish. Printing ink is the idea that completes this fact. Fertilizer would fill a different blank than printing ink.

q: Halogens ($F_2$, $Cl_2$, $Br_2$, $I_2$) are _____ molecules.
e: Halogens (F2, Cl2, Br2, I2) are diatomic molecules. Diatomic is the idea that completes this fact. Monatomic would fill a different blank than diatomic.

q: At room temperature, fluorine and chlorine are gases, bromine is a _____, and iodine is a solid.
e: At room temperature, fluorine and chlorine are gases, bromine is a liquid, and iodine is a solid. Liquid is the idea that completes this fact. Gas would fill a different blank than liquid.

q: The essential electronic structure of halogens is _____.
e: The essential electronic structure of halogens is ns2 np5. Ns2 np5 is the idea that completes this fact. Ns1 would fill a different blank than ns2 np5.

q: Among the halogens, _____ is the most reactive.
e: Among the halogens, fluorine is the most reactive. Fluorine is the idea that completes this fact. Chlorine would fill a different blank than fluorine.

q: In nature, halogens are found as salts of the _____.
e: In nature, halogens are found as salts of the halides. Halides is the idea that completes this fact. Oxides would fill a different blank than halides.

q: In the laboratory, halogen is prepared by heating sodium or potassium halide with manganese(IV) oxide and _____.
e: In the laboratory, halogen is prepared by heating sodium or potassium halide with manganese(IV) oxide and concentrated sulphuric acid. Concentrated sulphuric acid is the idea that completes this fact. Concentrated nitric acid would fill a different blank than concentrated sulphuric acid.

q: Chlorine is collected by the upward displacement of air because it is slightly soluble in water and _____ than air.
e: Chlorine is collected by the upward displacement of air because it is slightly soluble in water and heavier than air. Heavier is the idea that completes this fact. The same density as would fill a different blank than heavier.

q: Due to its _____ colour, chlorine gas can be seen easily when the gas jar is full.
e: Due to its greenish yellow colour, chlorine gas can be seen easily when the gas jar is full. Greenish yellow is the idea that completes this fact. Pale yellow would fill a different blank than greenish yellow.

q: If required dry, chlorine gas is passed into _____.
e: If required dry, chlorine gas is passed into concentrated sulphuric acid. Concentrated sulphuric acid is the idea that completes this fact. Dilute sulphuric acid would fill a different blank than concentrated sulphuric acid.

q: The chemical equation for the preparation of chlorine is _____.
e: The chemical equation for the preparation of chlorine is 2NaCl(s) + MnO2(s) + 3H2SO4(l) 2NaHSO4(aq) + MnSO4(aq) + Cl2(g) + 2H2O(l). 2NaCl(s) + MnO2(s) + 3H2SO4(l) 2NaHSO4(aq) + MnSO4(aq) + Cl2(g) + 2H2O(l) is the idea that completes this fact. NaCl + H2SO4 to NaHSO4 + HCl would fill a different blank than 2NaCl(s) + MnO2(s) + 3H2SO4(l) 2NaHSO4(aq) + MnSO4(aq) + Cl2(g) + 2H2O(l).

q: Fluorine is a very _____ gas.
e: Fluorine is a very pale yellow gas. Pale yellow is the idea that completes this fact. Reddish brown would fill a different blank than pale yellow.

q: Fluorine reacts with almost all other elements, except _____.
e: Fluorine reacts with almost all other elements, except helium and neon. Helium and neon is the idea that completes this fact. Oxygen and nitrogen would fill a different blank than helium and neon.

q: Chlorine is a _____ gas with a choking, unpleasant smell.
e: Chlorine is a pale green gas with a choking, unpleasant smell. Pale green is the idea that completes this fact. Purple-black would fill a different blank than pale green.

q: Chlorine is about _____ times as dense as air.
e: Chlorine is about 2.5 times as dense as air. 2.5 is the idea that completes this fact. 1.5 would fill a different blank than 2.5.

q: Bromine is a heavy, reddish brown, _____ liquid.
e: Bromine is a heavy, reddish brown, volatile liquid. Volatile is the idea that completes this fact. Non-volatile would fill a different blank than volatile.

q: Bromine is slightly soluble in water, forming a _____ solution containing about 3 percent of bromine at ordinary temperature.
e: Bromine is slightly soluble in water, forming a yellowish red solution containing about 3 percent of bromine at ordinary temperature. Yellowish red is the idea that completes this fact. Violet would fill a different blank than yellowish red.

q: Iodine is a _____ shiny solid with an irritating smell.
e: Iodine is a purple-black shiny solid with an irritating smell. Purple-black is the idea that completes this fact. Pale green would fill a different blank than purple-black.

q: Iodine sublimes rapidly when heated, forming a _____ vapour.
e: Iodine sublimes rapidly when heated, forming a violet vapour. Violet is the idea that completes this fact. Yellow would fill a different blank than violet.

q: Iodine is almost insoluble in water but readily dissolves in aqueous potassium iodide to form a _____ solution.
e: Iodine is almost insoluble in water but readily dissolves in aqueous potassium iodide to form a brown solution. Brown is the idea that completes this fact. Violet would fill a different blank than brown.

q: Iodine dissolves in carbon disulphide and carbon tetrachloride, forming _____ solutions.
e: Iodine dissolves in carbon disulphide and carbon tetrachloride, forming violet solutions. Violet is the idea that completes this fact. Green would fill a different blank than violet.

q: The reactivity of halogens occurs in the order of _____.
e: The reactivity of halogens occurs in the order of F2 > Cl2 > Br2 > I2. F2 > Cl2 > Br2 > I2 is the idea that completes this fact. Cl2 > F2 > Br2 > I2 would fill a different blank than F2 > Cl2 > Br2 > I2.

q: When a tube containing equal volumes of chlorine and hydrogen is exposed to sunlight, it _____.
e: When a tube containing equal volumes of chlorine and hydrogen is exposed to sunlight, it explodes. Explodes is the idea that completes this fact. Slowly reacts would fill a different blank than explodes.

q: Chlorine reacts vigorously with metals to form _____.
e: Chlorine reacts vigorously with metals to form metal chlorides. Metal chlorides is the idea that completes this fact. Metal hydrides would fill a different blank than metal chlorides.

q: When a very thin sheet of an alloy of copper and zinc is dropped into a chlorine gas jar, it burns brightly with a _____ flame.
e: When a very thin sheet of an alloy of copper and zinc is dropped into a chlorine gas jar, it burns brightly with a green flame. Green is the idea that completes this fact. Yellow would fill a different blank than green.

q: Phosphorus burns spontaneously in chlorine to form phosphorus(III) chloride and _____.
e: Phosphorus burns spontaneously in chlorine to form phosphorus(III) chloride and phosphorus(V) chloride. Phosphorus(V) chloride is the idea that completes this fact. Phosphorus hydride would fill a different blank than phosphorus(V) chloride.

q: Among halogens, chlorine and bromine have bleaching power, however, _____ does not.
e: Among halogens, chlorine and bromine have bleaching power, however, iodine does not. Iodine is the idea that completes this fact. Fluorine is among the listed items, so it is not the exception.

q: Chlorine reacts with water to form HOCl and _____.
e: Chlorine reacts with water to form HOCl and HCl. HCl is the idea that completes this fact. O2 would fill a different blank than HCl.

q: The HOCl slowly decomposes to hydrochloric acid and _____.
e: The HOCl slowly decomposes to hydrochloric acid and nascent oxygen. Oxygen supports respiration and combustion, and it is a very reactive non-metal. Chlorine gas would fill a different blank than nascent oxygen.

q: The nascent oxygen bleaches dyes by _____ them.
e: The nascent oxygen bleaches dyes by oxidising them. Oxidising is the idea that completes this fact. Reducing would fill a different blank than oxidising.

q: Chlorine will bleach moist litmus papers. This is used as a test for _____.
e: Chlorine will bleach moist litmus papers. This is used as a test for chlorine. Chlorine is the idea that completes this fact. Oxygen would fill a different blank than chlorine.

q: Halogens are _____ agents.
e: Halogens are oxidising agents. Oxidising is the idea that completes this fact. Reducing would fill a different blank than oxidising.

q: Chlorine oxidises iron(II) chloride into _____.
e: Chlorine oxidises iron(II) chloride into iron(III) chloride. Iron(III) chloride is the idea that completes this fact. Iron metal would fill a different blank than iron(III) chloride.

q: Iodine oxidises hydrogen sulphide to form hydrogen iodide and liberate _____.
e: Iodine oxidises hydrogen sulphide to form hydrogen iodide and liberate sulphur. Sulphur is the idea that completes this fact. Oxygen would fill a different blank than sulphur.

q: Chlorine reacts with cold dilute potassium hydroxide to form potassium chloride, potassium hypochlorite and _____.
e: Chlorine reacts with cold dilute potassium hydroxide to form potassium chloride, potassium hypochlorite and water. Water is the idea that completes this fact. Hydrogen would fill a different blank than water.

q: Chlorine reacts with hot concentrated potassium hydroxide to form potassium chloride, potassium chlorate and _____.
e: Chlorine reacts with hot concentrated potassium hydroxide to form potassium chloride, potassium chlorate and water. Water is the idea that completes this fact. Hydrogen would fill a different blank than water.

q: When chlorine is passed into a solution of sodium bromide, the respective halogen is displaced by more reactive chlorine to form sodium chloride and _____.
e: When chlorine is passed into a solution of sodium bromide, the respective halogen is displaced by more reactive chlorine to form sodium chloride and bromine. Bromine is the idea that completes this fact. Fluorine would fill a different blank than bromine.

q: When bromine is passed into a solution of sodium iodide, _____ is liberated.
e: When bromine is passed into a solution of sodium iodide, iodine is liberated. Iodine is the idea that completes this fact. Chlorine would fill a different blank than iodine.

q: Iodine cannot displace chlorine and bromine from their salt solutions because it is _____ reactive.
e: Iodine cannot displace chlorine and bromine from their salt solutions because it is less reactive. Less is the idea that completes this fact. More would fill a different blank than less.

q: A halide ion is a halogen atom with a _____ charge.
e: A halide ion is a halogen atom with a negative charge. Negative is the idea that completes this fact. Neutral would fill a different blank than negative.

q: The presence of chloride, bromide or iodide ions can be tested by adding _____ solution.
e: The presence of chloride, bromide or iodide ions can be tested by adding silver nitrate solution. Acidified silver nitrate is a test for chloride: a white precipitate of AgCl appears. Sodium hydroxide would fill a different blank than silver nitrate.

q: Samples for the silver nitrate test are typically acidified with dilute nitric acid to remove interfering ions, e.g., _____ ions.
e: Samples for the silver nitrate test are typically acidified with dilute nitric acid to remove interfering ions, e.g., carbonate ions. Carbonate is the idea that completes this fact. Nitrate would fill a different blank than carbonate.

q: In the silver nitrate test for halides, different colours of _____ precipitates are observed.
e: In the silver nitrate test for halides, different colours of silver halide precipitates are observed. Silver halide is the idea that completes this fact. Silver oxide would fill a different blank than silver halide.

q: Fluorine is used in the form of fluorides in drinking water to prevent tooth decay by hardening the _____ on teeth.
e: Fluorine is used in the form of fluorides in drinking water to prevent tooth decay by hardening the enamel on teeth. Enamel is the idea that completes this fact. Dentine would fill a different blank than enamel.

q: Chlorine is used to make PVC (Polyvinyl chloride) plastic as well as household _____.
e: Chlorine is used to make PVC (Polyvinyl chloride) plastic as well as household bleaches. Bleaches is the idea that completes this fact. Fuels would fill a different blank than bleaches.

q: Bromine is used to make disinfectants, medicines and _____.
e: Bromine is used to make disinfectants, medicines and fire retardants. Fire retardants is the idea that completes this fact. Glass would fill a different blank than fire retardants.

q: Iodine is used in medicines to treat cases of _____ and as a disinfectant (e.g., 'Tincture of iodine').
e: Iodine is used in medicines to treat cases of goiter and as a disinfectant (e.g., 'Tincture of iodine'). Goiter is the idea that completes this fact. Scurvy would fill a different blank than goiter.

q: Halides are widely used in metal halide lamps that are _____.
e: Halides are widely used in metal halide lamps that are high-intensity discharge lamps. High-intensity discharge lamps is the idea that completes this fact. Low-intensity discharge lamps would fill a different blank than high-intensity discharge lamps.
